title: Footsteps — Spring 2026
coverLines: Walk with Jesus for thirteen weeks
The way, the truth, the life
summary: Spring 2026 study guide for Surge: thirteen weeks of walking the Jesus way — the call, the beatitudes, the lower love, the cross, the sending. One verse and one daily read for every day of the season.

blocks.text: How to use this study guide

This is a Footsteps study guide for Surge. Spring has thirteen weeks, and each week we walk one stretch of the Jesus way: the call, blessed foundations, love that goes lower, truth that sets free, cross-shaped living, sending. Each day has a verse to read, two or three lines to think on, one honest Try it step, and a prayer. Bring your real life to the road — the way of Jesus is walked in shoes like yours.
The way

Jesus didn't come chiefly to give information; he came to open a way. A way of being human, of loving, of handling money and enemies and failure and ambition. Most of us didn't inherit that way we had to decide to walk it. This spring, thirteen weeks, one footprint a day — that's how a way becomes your way.

Follow the steps on each day: read the verse, read the lines, do the Try it, then pray. Day 5 of each week has a short quiz to check your bearings. Days 6 and 7 are for rest and reflection — walk slow, let it land. The Jesus way is not a sprint; it is a life.

intro.text: Every road begins with a call. Before the Jesus way is a set of teachings, it is a person saying 'come and see'. This week we start where the disciples started — at the invitation, not the syllabus.

verse.text: Come, and you will see.

blocks.text: Jesus' first recorded invitation is not a doctrine test but an open door: come and see. Andrew and the other disciple go, they stay, and their whole lives reroute. Following Jesus begins the same way for everyone — not with having it all figured out, but with showing up to look.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Act on 'come and see': actually show up to look at Jesus today
Spend ten minutes in one gospel, not as study — as seeing
Ask one honest question you've been afraid to bring to him

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Answer the call: Lord, I'm coming to see
Ask him to show you what you're walking toward

verse.text: "Come, follow me," Jesus said, "and I will send you out to fish for people."

blocks.text: Jesus calls fishermen into a new trade: fishing for people. The striking thing is that he calls them forward into a mission they don't understand yet — and they leave the nets on the shore. The call promises direction more than detail.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one net on your shore — something safe you're holding back from
Ask: what is Jesus actually inviting me into right now?
Take one step of yes today, even without the full map

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Say yes to his direction before you see his detail
Ask for the same courage the fishermen had

verse.text: So they left everything and followed him.

blocks.text: Luke adds the fuller cost: they left everything. Not a little. Everything. The call of Jesus is not to upgrade your life but to re-own it — from a thing you manage to a thing he sends. Leaving everything usually looks less dramatic and is no less real.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Make a short list of what 'everything' looks like for you this season
Choose one thing to place in his hands that you've been gripping
Don't romanticise it — just do the actual handover

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Hand Jesus the thing you've been managing
Thank him that what you leave is never loss

verse.text: Jesus looked at him and loved him.

blocks.text: Before the rich man gets the hardest invitation in the gospels — go, sell, give, come — he is looked at and loved. The call of Jesus is never a rejection notice. It can be costly; it is never cold.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Receive that look today: Jesus looks at you and loves you
Separate the cost of the call from the love behind it
Let his love give you the courage to hear the costly part honestly

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let Jesus look at you and love you first
Ask for courage to hear the full invitation

verse.text: You still lack one thing.

blocks.text: The rich young man has kept the rules, and Jesus names the gap: one thing — his money owns him, and he walks away sad. Today's quiz tests what we're really attached to when the call gets specific.

blocks.question: Why did Jesus tell the rich young man to sell what he had?
options: Because money is bad and must be destroyed
Because that one possession stood between him and following
blocks.explain: Right — the command was precision medicine. The 'one thing' was the one thing in the way.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to name your 'one thing' honestly
Pray for the courage to loosen your hold on it

verse.text: If you hold to my teaching, you are really my disciples.

blocks.text: The road is not walked in a day; it is walked by holding to his teaching — a verb that means staying, remaining, abiding. On a rest day, let the pace slow. The call was never 'arrive'; it was 'abide'.

blocks.prompt: What has the week's call surfaced that you need to sit with — not solve yet? Write it in one honest paragraph.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to abide in his teaching today
Thank him that discipleship is a staying, not a sprinting

days.title: Written in the book of life

verse.text: Instead, rejoice that your names are written in heaven.

blocks.text: The seventy return from mission amazed at their power, and Jesus redirects their joy: the real wonder is not what you can do but whose you are — your name written in heaven. On Monday, set your anchor on identity before activity.

blocks.prompt: Before the week's doing starts: what does it mean to you that your name is written in heaven? Write it down.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rejoice that your name is written in heaven
Ask him to order your doing after your belonging

intro.text: The Beatitudes are the blueprint of the Jesus way — blessings, not conditions. This week we lay the foundations that the rest of the road is built on.

verse.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

blocks.text: The beatitudes begin at the bottom, not the top: blessed are the poor in spirit — those who admit they don't have enough strength, wisdom or holiness to save themselves. It's the opposite of spiritual hustling. The kingdom is for the people who know they need it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Admit one small poverty out loud: somewhere you simply don't have it
Stop performing spiritual competence with God today
Notice the relief in being poor in spirit before him

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Come to God in your poverty, not your impressive
Thank him that the kingdom goes to the empty-handed

verse.text: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.

blocks.text: Jesus blesses mourners at the front of his manifesto — a culture-changing act. Grief over what's broken, what's lost, what's wrong in the world is not a failure of faith; it is the precondition for comfort. You can't be comforted for something you refuse to feel.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let yourself actually grieve one thing — there are no points for stoic
Refuse the cynicism that turns grief into jokes
Ours is the God who promises comfort, not just lectures

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Bring your mourning to the God who comforts
Ask for comfort — real comfort — not just distraction

verse.text: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

blocks.text: Meekness has been misread as weakness, but it is strength under control — a stallion when it could be a bulldozer. The meek inherit the earth because they don't have to conquer it; they know the earth already belongs to God and are content to receive it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Hold your strength in check in one situation where you could crush
Give up being the smartest person in the room
Be content to inherit rather than to conquer

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the meekness of strength under control
Thank God that the earth is his to give

verse.text: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.

blocks.text: Righteousness is not a distant cool concept here — it is the one thing you want as badly as food and water. Jesus blesses raw appetite. A craving for what's right — in you, in your city, in your workplace — is the sign of a healthy soul, and Jesus promises it gets satisfied.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let yourself actually want what is right — don't apologise for the appetite
Do one righteous (not just legal) thing today
Ask for more hunger, not less

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Bring your hunger for rightness to Jesus
Trust his promise: you will be filled

verse.text: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.

blocks.text: The beatitudes keep going lower: mercy. The merciful are those who have been hurt and choose not to scoreboard it. Today's quiz checks which road actually leads to the heart of the beatitudes.

blocks.question: Why does the 'way of Jesus' start with blessings on the meek and poor in spirit?
options: Because the way is built on receiving, not achieving
Because God admires self-made strength
blocks.explain: Right — the whole way of Jesus is grounded in grace: blessed are the people who come empty, not the ones who compete their way up.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to grow mercy in you the way it grew in him
Thank him that mercy is received before it is given

verse.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.

blocks.text: Purity of heart is not perfection of record; it is singleness of intention — one thing you want above the clutter. On a rest day, let the filters settle. What is the one thing you actually want? The pure in heart are on the way to seeing God.

blocks.prompt: Confession moment: what is competing with God for your heart's singularity? Write it down and give it a name.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for a clean, single-hearted desire
Anticipate the blessing: you will see God

verse.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

blocks.text: The foundation week closes with the family resemblance: peacemakers are called children of God because they act like their Father, who makes peace. On Monday, go make peace in one place — not by winning, by building.

blocks.prompt: Where is there a broken peace you can begin building today — an apology, a bridge, an honest conversation? Write your next step.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to bear your Father's family likeness today
Thank him that peacemakers are his own

intro.text: The world climbs; the Jesus way descends. This week we walk the radical centre of Jesus' teaching: love that goes lower — to servants, to strangers, to enemies.

verse.text: He got up from the meal, took off his outer clothing, and wrapped a towel around his waist.

blocks.text: The night before he is crucified, Jesus kneels and washes feet — the job reserved for the lowest servant. The King of the universe does the job nobody would do. Everything you will follow in the Jesus way is hidden in that towel: love expressed as descent.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Do the literal equivalent: pick up the job no one should have to
Let yourself be served — the other half of washing feet
Check your heart's altitude: are you descending today?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus for the towel, the basin and the descent
Ask him to make your love walk downward

days.title: I have set you an example

verse.text: I have set you an example that you should do as I have done for you.

blocks.text: Jesus doesn't just warm our hearts with the gesture; he hands us the basin. Do as I have done. Love that goes lower is not a feeling to admire; it's an assignment. Put on the towel.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Serve someone who can never pay you back
Let your leadership be towel-led, not title-led
Ask: what does 'as I have done' mean in my actual day?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive his example as your assignment
Ask for joy in the descent — not just duty

verse.text: Love your neighbour as yourself.

blocks.text: The command is ordinary-sounding until you define neighbour. Jesus demolishes every border the word 'neighbour' usually draws. It is not whoever is easy or like you — it's whoever is in front of you, in need. Even the ones you'd rather cross the street to avoid.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let the definition of neighbour expand by one category today
Love one stranger with the energy you usually save for friends
Include yourself in 'as yourself' — that's the baseline, not the prize

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to redefine your neighbours
Thank him that he treated himself as ordinary love demands you be treated

verse.text: Just as I have loved you, you also should love one another.

blocks.text: Jesus upgrades the old command: love one another 'as I have loved you' — with the towel, the basin, the willingness to go low when it costs. A group of believers that loves like that is the most dangerous sign on earth.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Wash someone's feet — literally or figuratively — today
Choose the low seat at the gathering, not the important one
Protect the dignity of someone who's been brought low

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the grace to love as Jesus loved
Thank him for the new commandment that is not new at all

verse.text: But I tell you, love your enemies.

blocks.text: This is the hardest line in the sermon, and Jesus doesn't soften it. Love your enemies — the ones who've hurt you, opposed you, wronged your people. Today's quiz is about what loving an enemy does not mean.

blocks.question: What does 'love your enemies' NOT mean?
options: Pretending the hurt never happened
Praying for their good and refusing to repay evil with evil
blocks.explain: Right — loving enemies is not denial; it is a disciplined refusal to let them write your heart's programming.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Name an enemy to Jesus and pray for their good
Ask for power to break the cycle of repayment

verse.text: Go and do likewise.

blocks.text: The lawyer gets the story's final order: go and do likewise — be the neighbour, even to the person your society trains you to walk past. On a rest day, rest includes readiness: the story is always waiting to be re-enacted in your week.

blocks.prompt: Who is your 'roadside' person — the one your world steps around? Write how a towel-shaped love might meet them this month.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to be the neighbour without borders
Thank Jesus for being the neighbour you didn't deserve

verse.text: This is how we know what love is: Jesus Christ laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers and sisters.

blocks.text: Here is the definition and the reach of the lower love: he laid down his life; we lay down ours — daily, for real people, in real doses. Monday is the day to rehearse your own small death: a pride, a plan, a preference, laid down for someone.

blocks.prompt: What would 'laying down your life' concretely mean this month? Write one specific act and put it in your calendar.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Contemplate the love that laid down his life
Ask for strength to lay yours down in real doses

intro.text: The Jesus way is allergic to masks. This week we walk in the truth that sets free: honesty with God, honesty with ourselves, honesty with one another.

verse.text: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.

blocks.text: Truth is not a burden to survive here; it is the key. You will know the truth, and it will set you free. The most common bondage in the modern soul is not lack of information but lack of honesty — we lie to ourselves and wonder why we're stuck.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Tell one true thing to God today — the unedited version
Name the lie you've been privately rehearsing
Choose truth over the smoother story in one conversation

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask the Spirit of truth to search your corners
Thank God that knowing the truth actually sets you free

verse.text: Instead, speaking the truth in love, we will grow to become in every respect the mature body of him who is the head, that is, Christ.

blocks.text: Truth without love is cruelty; love without truth is haze. Paul unites the two into one verb: speaking the truth in love — the way you grow up and the way the church grows up. One without the other just doesn't mature anything.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Say one hard true thing — in love, not in frustration
Receive a hard true thing without building walls
Check your mix: is your kindness costing the truth?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for truth that travels in love
Thank God that he wants both, not either

verse.text: I am the way and the truth and the life.

blocks.text: Jesus doesn't just teach truth; he claims to be it. The way you walk this spring is a person, the truth you know is a person, the life you're given is a person. That changes everything about how you hold 'truth' — it is met, not just mastered.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Meet the truth today more than you measure it
Stop using truth as a weapon and start letting it set you free
Take one step on the way that is a person

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Worship Jesus as the way, the truth, the life
Ask him to be known, not just studied

verse.text: If we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another.

blocks.text: John's picture of honesty: walking in the light — things visible, nothing curated for the dark. The surprise is that this is where fellowship lives. Hidden things separate; shared things connect.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Bring one hidden thing into the light today
Offer someone your honest story, not your highlight reel
Enjoy the strange lightness of nothing to manage

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for courage to walk in the light
Thank God that his light covers, not exposes, those who come to him

verse.text: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed.

blocks.text: James turns confession into a healing practice between people, not just a private transaction with God. Today's quiz is about the strange medicine of honest confession.

blocks.question: Why does James connect confession with healing?
options: Hidden sin keeps you sick; brought to light, it can be prayed over and healed
Confession is only for the faint-hearted
blocks.explain: Right — secrecy breeds infection; confession opens the wound to prayer and the balm of community.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Pray for the courage of honest confession
Ask for healing where secrets have made you sick

verse.text: Create in me a pure heart, O God.

blocks.text: David's post-failure prayer is the prayer of the honest soul: create in me a pure heart. He doesn't defend; he asks for reconstruction. On a rest day, let the truth do its work — the psalmists call it a clean heart, and it is the rest of the honest.

blocks.prompt: Write the prayer of a pure heart in your own words. What are you asking God to create in you?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Pray David's prayer for a pure heart
Trust that honesty with God is never the wrong door

verse.text: The LORD detests lying lips, but he delights in people who are trustworthy.

blocks.text: The way of truth ends where it began: a choice between two identities — the lying lips and the trustworthy heart. God delights in trustworthy people. On Monday, resolve to be one: true in the little things, and therefore true in the big ones.

blocks.prompt: Where are you tempted to trim the truth in small ways? Write the places — and your resolve for each.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to be someone God delights in — trustworthy
Thank him for truth, the surgery that sets free

intro.text: Jesus talked about money more than almost anything because money is where the heart sets its real coordinates. This week we walk the way of the kingdom through the myth that you can't be spiritual and financial.

verse.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

blocks.text: Jesus doesn't say your heart directs your treasure; he says your treasure directs your heart. Your bank statement is a spiritual autobiography whether you intend it or not. The Jesus way starts with honesty about where the treasure is going.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Do the uncomfortable audit: what do your spending patterns confess?
Move one unit of treasure toward Jesus' priorities today
Ask where your heart has actually been living

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Hand Jesus the ledger of your heart
Ask for hearts anchored where your treasure should be

verse.text: You cannot serve both God and money.

blocks.text: Jesus frames money as a rival god, not a tool. Money is not neutral; it is a loyalty that wants worship — security, status, control. The Jesus way dethrones it, not by pretending it doesn't exist but by refusing it the throne.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Worship-check: where did you look for safety today — God or money?
Practice a small act of financial risk-trust (give, lend, bless)
Refuse one fear-based decision led by money

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Reaffirm: serve God, not money
Ask for freedom from money's grip on your decisions

verse.text: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; do not trust your cleverness.

blocks.text: The proverb sounds cynical but is simply honest: money is a restless bird — it sprouts wings and flies off. Investing your life in the chasing of it is a treadmill with no exit. Wisdom refuses to be hypnotised by the flight of riches.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Refuse one 'get rich quick' thought today as a matter of principle
Invest in one thing that doesn't sprout wings: a person, a skill, the kingdom
Talk honestly with a friend about money — grieve the taboo

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for wisdom where money is concerned
Thank God that he is wealth that cannot flee

verse.text: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much.

blocks.text: Jesus teaches that money management is trust management. The way you handle the little (however little) is exactly how God tests what he can entrust to you. Faithfulness precedes favour.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Manage some 'little' with utter faithfulness today — time, a small sum, a duty
Ask: what would faithful stewardship look like if nothing was 'mine'?
Let integrity in money speak louder than your talk about it

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to be trusted with little so you can be trusted with much
Thank God that he is the owner; you are the steward

verse.text: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moths and vermin do not destroy.

blocks.text: There is a bank that inflation, moths and market crashes can't touch: heaven. Today's quiz is about the wisdom of the two treasuries.

blocks.question: What is the practical test of where you're storing treasure?
options: How much you give away — treasure you can't keep anyway
How little you spend on yourself
blocks.explain: Right — heavenly treasure is a giving kind. The test is not austerity; it is direction.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask where your treasure is truly piling up
Thank God for a treasure that vermin cannot touch

verse.text: Come with me by yourselves to a quiet place and get some rest.

blocks.text: Even Jesus pulled his disciples out of the pace for a quiet rest. The kingdom is not fuelled by burnout. On a rest day, let the chassis cool — away from the metrics, the comparisons, the to-do list. Rest is not a reward; it's a royal entitlement.

blocks.prompt: Write down what rest actually looks like for you now — not a luxury plan, a real one. What would Jesus tell you to lay down today?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Come to the quiet place with Jesus
Thank him that rest is built into the kingdom's economy

verse.text: Remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.

blocks.text: Moses warns Israel, as they enter wealth: don't forget the Giver of the producing power. Every salary, salary-increase, opportunity and skill is downstream from God's giving. On Monday, steward the wealth — and remember where the ability came from.

blocks.prompt: What ability to produce have you been given? Treasure it this week — and give thanks for the Giver behind your game.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the ability to produce
Ask him to guard your heart from forgetting the Giver

intro.text: Prayer is not a slot in your schedule; it is the way you breathe on the Jesus way. This week we practise the kind of prayer Jesus taught — honest, persistent, trusting.

verse.text: This, then, is how you should pray: "Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name."

blocks.text: The model prayer begins with address, not agenda: our Father. Not 'my' — ours, a family prayer. Hevenly, hallowed. Before a single request, Jesus re-establishes who you are talking to: your Father, whose name you love.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Start prayer with address today: 'Our Father' — and mean it
Pray with someone else's need on your mind, not just yours
Slow down the opening: hallow his name before you ask anything

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Come to your Father as a family member
Ask that his name be revered in your life

verse.text: Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you.

blocks.text: Three verbs, one promise, and all of them are active. God is not inviting passive wishing; he is inviting persistent engagement — ask, seek, knock. The repetition is the point: the door opens to those who keep on coming.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Ask — out loud, specifically, for a real thing
Seek — take one actual search step toward your answer
Knock — don't give up after the first silence

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Bring your specific ask to your Father
Trust the promise: keep, seek, knock today

verse.text: Because this widow keeps bothering me, I will see that she gets justice.

blocks.text: Jesus tells a story of a widow who wears down a crooked judge — and then contrasts: if an unjust judge finally answers, how much more will a righteous Father? The point is not that God needs nagging; it's that persistence is the shape of faith.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Refuse to stop praying for one long-running thing
Let the widow's stubbornness be your model, not your embarrassment
Ask yourself: have I really persisted, or given up quietly?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Lay your one persistent request before the righteous judge
Thank him that he is not a grudging judge but a Father

verse.text: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. We do not know what we ought to pray for, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us.

blocks.text: There is enormous relief in this verse: you don't always know what to pray. When words fail, the Spirit prays in you with groans deeper than language. Prayer is not a performance art; it is a partnership.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give voice to a prayer you can't articulate — let the Spirit interpret
Admit your weakness in prayer out loud — it's the Spirit's cue
Pray through silence sometimes; groans count

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let the Spirit pray in your weakness today
Thank him that he intercedes when you can't find words

verse.text: He withdrew... and prayed.

blocks.text: The busiest man in the gospels kept withdrawing to pray. Jesus' rhythm of life was built on it — not prayer squeezed around a full schedule but the schedule built on prayer. Today's quiz is about Jesus' prayer practice.

blocks.question: What pattern did Jesus model in his busiest seasons?
options: Cutting prayer because the demands were urgent
Withdrawing to pray before and during the demands
blocks.explain: Right — Jesus made withdrawal to pray, not the workload, the foundation of his priorities.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Withdraw deliberately to pray
Follow Jesus into the quiet before the demands

verse.text: My soul finds rest in God alone.

blocks.text: Prayer is not only petition; it is resting your soul in God like a patient on a table. On a rest day, let prayer be less about raising hands with requests and more about letting go of everything you were gripping.

blocks.prompt: Sit in stillness for five minutes. What does your soul say when it isn't performing? Write two sentences.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest your soul in God alone
Thank him that prayer's deepest posture is trust

verse.text: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, faithful in prayer.

blocks.text: Paul's triple rhythm runs on the third rail: faithful in prayer. It is the current that keeps joy from curdling and patience from snapping. Monday is the day to wire prayer into your week like a power cable, not an ornament.

blocks.prompt: Write your practical prayer plan for the week: when, where, and the one thing you will persist on.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Commit to faithfulness in prayer this week
Thank God that the Spirit is in it with you

intro.text: Halfway through spring we walk to the centre: the cross. The Jesus way runs through it — not as decoration but as the shape of a surrendered life.

verse.text: Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.

blocks.text: In Jesus' world a cross was one thing — an instrument of execution, carried by a condemned man to his own death. He invites followers to the same posture: deny yourself, take it up, follow. The way of Jesus is a death-sentence life and the only one worth living.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one self-centred default you can deny today
Pick up the daily cross: the obedience you'd rather avoid
Follow — not negotiate — today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive the invitation to the cross-shaped life
Ask for the grace to deny yourself and follow

verse.text: Yet not as I will, but as you will.

blocks.text: In Gethsemane Jesus prays the most honest prayer ever prayed: Father, if it's possible, take this cup — and then, not as I will but as you will. The cross-shaped life is not the absence of preference; it is preference surrendered.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Say honestly to God what you'd prefer — then surrender it
Practise the two-clause prayer: my will, then yours
Let surrender be a daily rhythm, not a one-time event

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Bring your honest preference to the Father
End every prayer where Jesus ended his: not my will, but yours

verse.text: He humbled himself by becoming obedient to death — even death on a cross!

blocks.text: Paul gives the descent its full depth: Jesus did not merely serve or teach or wash feet — he humbled himself to death, even death on a cross. The cross is the bottom of the descent, and it is where the way of Jesus is measured. How low will love go?

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Trade a right you're entitled to for the sake of another today
Study the cross and let it reset your ambitions
Serve someone as if humility were still trending

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Contemplate the humility that went to the cross
Ask for the same mind that was in Christ Jesus

verse.text: When he had received the drink, Jesus said, "It is finished."

blocks.text: The cross is where striving ends. It is finished — the debt paid, the work completed, the verdict rendered. The cross-shaped life is not 'try harder to be saved'; it is 'already saved, now live it'. Your performance on the way is love's response, not the wage.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Stop earning what is already finished
Live today as someone already forgiven — light, not striving
Let the finished work end one of your self-condemnation loops

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive the finished work of the cross
Thank Jesus that the debt is paid in full

verse.text: I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me.

blocks.text: Paul's audacious claim: the old life is dead, executed with Jesus; what lives now is Christ in him. Today's quiz tests which 'I' died at the cross.

blocks.question: According to Galatians 2:20, what died with Christ?
options: The old self that lived for itself
The desire to ever experience difficulty
blocks.explain: Right — 'I have been crucified with Christ': the old ruler, the self-life, was executed. The life that remains is Christ's in you.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rehearse the exchange: dead to self, alive to Christ
Ask Christ to live so evidently in you

verse.text: Later, knowing that everything had now been finished, and so that Scripture would be fulfilled, Jesus said, "I am thirsty."

blocks.text: Even his thirst was completion. On a rest day, let the cross do its quiet work: every burden you carry about your worth, your standing, your failures — finished. Rest is not earned at the foot of this cross; it is received.

blocks.prompt: What are you still trying to 'finish' that Jesus already declared finished? Write it down — then receive it as finished.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest at the foot of the finished cross
Thank Jesus that every 'it is finished' is for you

verse.text: May I never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

blocks.text: The cross-shaped life has one boast: the cross. Not your resume, your church attendance, your moral record — but the executed Son and his finished grace. On Monday, choose your boast and let it reorder the week.

blocks.prompt: What have you been quietly boasting in? Swap it today for the only boast that holds — write the swap down.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Boast in the cross of Christ alone today
Thank him for the humility that funds your salvation

weeks.title: Week 8 — Faith for the long road

intro.text: Spring faith is easy; the long road of a lifetime is where it's tested. This week we walk the endurance of faith — waiting, hoping, not giving up, keeping first things first.

verse.text: Now faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.

blocks.text: The long road runs on two rails: confidence in what is hoped for, assurance about what is not yet seen. Faith is not certainty about details; it is settled trust in the Character behind the promises. That trust is the road beneath your feet.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name what you hope for — confidently, not wishfully
Hold assurance for what you cannot yet see
Choose trust in the Character, not certainty on the details

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the confidence of faith today
Thank God for being trustworthy on the unseen road

verse.text: If you have faith as small as a mustard seed... Nothing will be impossible for you.

blocks.text: The disciples ask why they couldn't drive out the demon, and Jesus points to the tiny seed: faith the size of a mustard seed. Faith is not about magnitude; it's about placement — a small amount resting fully on a large God.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Bring your small, honest faith — not a pretend big one
Stop measuring faith by feelings and start by obedience
Act on the seed you have; it's enough

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Present your mustard seed to the God of the impossible
Thank him that he works with small and honest faith

verse.text: Let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us.

blocks.text: The long road is a race 'marked out for us' — not a race we choose, but the one appointed. And it is run with perseverance: the unglamorous stamina of showing up again. The witnesses in the stands (the previous chapter's hall of faith) know how it ends.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Receive your marked-out race without resentful comparisons
Define success as persistence, not position
Run today's lap — you don't have to run tomorrow's

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for perseverance, the gift of the long haul
Thank God for the cloud of witnesses rooting you on

verse.text: Fixing our eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of faith.

blocks.text: The antidote to giving up: fixed eyes. Not on the difficulty, not even on your faith, but on Jesus — the pioneer who went first and the perfecter who completes what he started. The road holds because the eyes hold.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: When the road feels endless, return your eyes to Jesus
Follow the pioneer: he has walked every stretch before you
Trust the perfecter: he finishes what he starts

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Fix your eyes on the pioneer and perfecter
Thank Jesus for going first and finishing last

verse.text: Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off everything that hinders.

blocks.text: You are not the first, or the last. Hebrews 11 lists the long-distance runners of faith — Abraham, Moses, Rahab — and says they surround you like a stadium. Today's quiz is on where a long-distance runner gets their assurance.

blocks.question: What let the heroes of faith endure the unseen road?
options: Seeing their reward in the crowd's approval
Seeing him who is invisible, and trusting the promise
blocks.explain: Right — Hebrews says Moses 'persevered because he saw him who is invisible'. Assurance is about the unseen God, not the visible crowd.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Honour the witnesses who have run before you
Ask for strength to follow their footsteps home

verse.text: In repentance and rest is your salvation, in quietness and trust is your strength.

blocks.text: The long road has a built-in pace: rest. Isaiah calls it quietness and trust — not the exhaustion of speed but the staying-power of rest in God. On a rest day, receive the gift that rescues you from burnout's slow sabotage.

blocks.prompt: Where have you been running on fumes? Write where rest — real rest — needs to re-enter your weekly rhythm.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive quietness and trust as your strength
Thank God that rest is the pace of the long road

verse.text: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.

blocks.text: Paul ends his life with the threefold finish-line report: fought the good fight, finished the race, kept the faith. Not 'won every round' but 'kept the faith'. Monday is for making peace with the race being long and the finish being faithful, not flawless.

blocks.prompt: Write what 'kept the faith' would look like at the end of your life. What does that change about this week?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the grace to finish faithful
Thank God for the crown that waits for those who love his appearing

intro.text: Unforgiveness is a weight that grows in the dark. This week we walk the hardest freedom in the kingdom: forgiveness without limit — for the family, the church, and the people who have hurt you most.

verse.text: I tell you, not seven times, but seventy-seven times.

blocks.text: Peter offers his ceiling — seven times, generous by any standard — and Jesus explodes the counting: seventy-seven. The point is not arithmetic but disposition: stop keeping the books. Unforgiveness always starts bookkeeping; forgiveness starts ledger-burning.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find a tally you've been keeping and burn it
Forgive a person again for the same offence — that's the seventy-seven way
Ask: who am I still 'not' forgiving?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the grace to stop counting
Thank God whose forgiveness already tore up your ledger

verse.text: Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.

blocks.text: The model prayer installs a terrifying link: we are forgiven as we forgive. Not before, not after — as. It's not a wage for your goodness but a mirror of your reception. A forgiven person is, by nature, a forgiving one.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Before you ask forgiveness, examine your own forgiving
Pray the prayer and mean the clause: 'as we forgive'
Release a debtor today — financial, relational, emotional

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for forgiveness with open, forgiving hands
Thank God for the 'as' — the mirror of grace

days.title: Forgive as the Lord forgave you

verse.text: Bear with each other and forgive one another... as the Lord forgave you.

blocks.text: The standard is scandalous: forgive as the Lord forgave you. He forgave before you asked, fully and without keeping a receipt. That's the model. Anything smaller is not the Jesus way; anything approximating it is supernatural.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Forgive before the apology arrives
Forgive without presenting the receipt
Receive it yourself: how did Christ forgive you?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for forgiveness that mirrors his
Thank him for the size of grace you are modelling

verse.text: Shouldn't you have had mercy on your fellow servant just as I had on you?

blocks.text: The parable's bookkeeping: a servant forgiven a fortune refuses his colleague a handful of coins. The master's question is the sharpest in the gospels. Unforgiveness is not just a cold heart; it is amnesia about grace.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Measure the size of grace you've received — then release the small debt
Recall a specific forgiveness God gave you; let it disarm your grudge
Practise mercy toward the one you find hardest

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Re-memorise your own massive forgiveness
Ask to refuse the trap of the unforgiving servant

verse.text: First go and be reconciled.

blocks.text: Jesus says the priority of the gift-bearer: before you even offer your gift at the altar, go and be reconciled. Worship and reconciliation belong together. Today's quiz tests the radical order Jesus sets.

blocks.question: According to Matthew 5:23-24, what comes first?
options: The offering, then reconciliation later, if practical
Go and reconcile — before the gift
blocks.explain: Right — Jesus orders reconciliation ahead of ritual. A broken relationship is a blocked offering.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Identify the reconciliation that awaits your next step
Ask for courage to go first

verse.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

blocks.text: God's forgiveness has distance and direction: east from west — infinite, non-intersecting. On a rest day, let your own heaviness be removed that far. If God no longer sees it, why are you still carrying it?

blocks.prompt: What old guilt are you hauling that God has already removed? Write the phrase, tear it up, and let the distance stand.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive the east-west removal of your sin
Thank God your forgiven record is beyond retrieval

verse.text: Freely you have received; freely give.

blocks.text: The kingdom economy in four words: freely received, freely given. Forgiveness is how you pass along the only wealth that has no end. On Monday, give somebody a gift that cost you your pride — and feel the freedom of the debtor set loose.

blocks.prompt: Write the name of the person you will forgiveness-forward to this week, and the step you'll take. This is the ledger's last page.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give freely because you received freely
Thank God for the forgiveness that funds yours

intro.text: Jesus announced a kingdom that has drawn near and lives inside. This week we walk that inward kingdom — the Spirit at work, the fruit it grows, the new heart it makes.

verse.text: The kingdom of God is in your midst.

blocks.text: The kingdom is not a distant flag to await; it has drawn near. It works like leaven, lives like seed, and takes up residence where Jesus reigns — in you. Politics and powers come and go; the kingdom in the heart is the one that changes everything.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let the King reign in one decision today
Act as if the kingdom, not the newsfeed, is the real government
Ask: where is the kingdom already growing in me?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask the King to reign within you today
Thank God for a kingdom that has drawn near

verse.text: The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, till it was all leavened.

blocks.text: The kingdom grows like bread rising — hidden, slow, irreversible, and working its way through everything. You don't need to see the leaven to see the bread. The fruit of a life taken over by the kingdom is eventually unmistakable.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Hold on to a hidden work you can't yet see rising
Let kingdom influence permeate one area you've barricaded
Trust time: leaven doesn't rise in a day

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the hidden, sure growth of his kingdom
Ask for patience with what is rising slowly

verse.text: Very truly I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again.

blocks.text: Nicodemus, a learned man, stands in the dark trying to understand, and Jesus says the kingdom starts with a birth, not a course. The new birth is not a self-improvement; it is a new origin. Everything about the kingdom in you is downstream from it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Stop trying to earn entry to the kingdom — receive your birth
Look at your life differently: born of the Spirit, not of effort
Ask honestly: have I been born again, or only informed?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the new birth in the Spirit
Ask for eyes to see the kingdom you've been born into

verse.text: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.

blocks.text: The kingdom in you produces nine fruits — and notice it's singular 'fruit', one crop. These are not nine resolutions; they are the natural yield of a tree indwelt by the Spirit. You don't manufacture fruit; you remain in the tree.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Pick one fruit to examine today — how does it grow in you?
Stop producing, start remaining in the Vine
Thank the Spirit for what He is growing despite your drought

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask the Spirit to grow his fruit in you
Thank him for a crop you cannot force

verse.text: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!

blocks.text: The kingdom in you is not renovated; it is recreated. Today's quiz tests what the new creation actually changed.

blocks.question: What does it mean that you are a 'new creation' in Christ?
options: Your old self is gone and a new life has begun
You're the same person with better behaviour
blocks.explain: Right — 'the old has gone, the new is here' is a change of identity, not a behaviour patch.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive the new creation identity
Thank God the old is gone and the new is here

verse.text: Seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.

blocks.text: The kingdom's priorities free you from the scramble. Seeking first changes the order of a whole life, and the promise covers the rest like a blanket. On a rest day, lay still under the blanket: what is first is settled, so you can rest.

blocks.prompt: What have you been putting first that belongs lower down? Write one reversal to practise this week.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Seek first his kingdom, and rest in the rest
Thank God for provision that follows priority

verse.text: Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

blocks.text: The kingdom in you is not escapism; it is a prayer with consequences — your will be done on earth as in heaven. The kingdom has arrived inside you so it can leak out into your home, your work, your city. On Monday, be the place where heaven leaks.

blocks.prompt: Where in your world is 'as it is in heaven' most clearly missing — and what is one kingdom act you can bring there this week?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Pray the kingdom down and live it out
Thank God the kingdom is in you and for the world

intro.text: The Jesus way is not walked alone. This week we walk to the table Jesus set — communion with him and with each other — and to the joining that becomes a people.

verse.text: Take and eat; this is my body.

blocks.text: At the last supper Jesus takes bread and gives it away: this is my body. He gives himself as food for a journey. Communion is not a religious snack; it is the unforgettable rendezvous where the way of Jesus is nourished at its source.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Receive communion this week as nourishment, not obligation
Remember that what is given is a body — his, for you
Let the table re-centre one of your distractions

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus for the bread that is his body
Ask to be fed by him for the road ahead

days.title: This cup is the new covenant

verse.text: This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.

blocks.text: The cup inaugurates a new covenant — not a contract you keep but a bond he established in blood. It 'is poured out for many'. The table is the great equaliser: every head bowed at it is a recipient, no one a founder.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Drink the cup as covenant, not ceremony
Include 'the many' in your sitting at the table
Refuse the pride of the self-made religious

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus for the blood of the new covenant
Ask to live from the covenant, not toward it

verse.text: Do this in remembrance of me.

blocks.text: Jesus commissions a habit: do this in remembrance. The table is the church's rehearsal — remembering the death until he comes. Lent, Easter, ordinary Tuesdays — the remembering has to be practised or it fades into a doctrine about him instead of a meeting with him.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let one practical act today be 'in remembrance'
Let the memory of his death precede your self-pity
Practise the remembering that keeps him present

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to remember him until he comes
Thank him for making remembering a gift, not a guilt

verse.text: Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.

blocks.text: Joined to Christ and therefore joined to each other: your invitation to the table is an invitation into a body. You are not an audience member of the Jesus way; you are a functioning part of his people — with a job only you can do.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find and use your part in the body today
Honour a part of the body that isn't you
Stop attending church; start being the body

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for making you a member of Christ's body
Ask for the grace to belong and to serve

verse.text: For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them.

blocks.text: The table people are a gathering people. Jesus promises his presence where two or three gather — not to a full stadium, not to a minimum headcount, just to two or three in his name. Today's quiz is about the size of the joining.

blocks.question: What does Jesus promise where two or three gather in his name?
options: That his presence is there among them
That their gathering will grow impressive
blocks.explain: Right — the promise is presence, not multiplication. The joining is about him being with them.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Gather with two or three in his name
Thank him that his presence is the whole gathering

verse.text: In my Father's house are many rooms.

blocks.text: Communion on earth points to a longer table: my Father's house has many rooms. The way home is not a scramble for a bed — rooms are already prepared. On a rest day, let the table's future hope settle your present anxiety.

blocks.prompt: What does the promise of 'many rooms' do to your current fear about belonging? Write the shift.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest in the Father's prepared rooms
Thank Jesus he went ahead to prepare your place

verse.text: A new command I give you: love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another.

blocks.text: The table sends you to one another on a new command: love one another as I have loved you. The joining is not a club; it's an order of lovers. On Monday, love the ones at your table with the exact love you've received there.

blocks.prompt: Who sits at your table, worktable, phone table — who needs the love you received at his table? Write one act of it for this week.
blocks.placeholder: Loved at his table, I will love...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive the love that gives itself as food
Ask to love as you have been loved

intro.text: The Jesus way ends in sending. In the last week of walking, Jesus turns his followers from students into sent ones — carrying grace to the whole world from where they live.

verse.text: Go and make disciples of all nations.

blocks.text: The final command is a sending: go and make disciples. Not 'come and sit' but 'go and make'. The way of Jesus was always going to have to travel — through you, from your town, to all nations. Discipleship is the multiplier.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Receive your sending — you are sent, not just saved
Name your 'nations': the specific people only you can reach
Take one small step of going today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Accept the send-off you have been given
Ask for nations — near and far — on your heart

verse.text: And you will be my witnesses... to the ends of the earth.

blocks.text: Jesus sequences the sending with geography: Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, the ends of the earth. The witness always starts where you are — your street, your family, your workplace — and radiates outward. You don't skip your Jerusalem.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Start with your Jerusalem: one witness at home or in your street
Then Judea: your town's edges, your workplace
Keep praying wider — Samaria, the ends of the earth

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to be a bold witness in your Jerusalem first
Thank God your sending begins close to home

verse.text: My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations.

blocks.text: The vision goes back further than you think: God's plan was always all nations. Your sending is not an appendix to the gospel; it is the gospel's native language. The house of God is a house built with the doors open.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Pray for one believer suffering for the faith overseas
Widen your welcome to include people 'of all nations' in your town
Let your church be a house of prayer, not a house of the familiar

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Pray for all nations today
Thank God for the global family your welcome should reach

verse.text: The harvest is plentiful but the workers are few.

blocks.text: Jesus looks at the crowds with compassion — harassed and helpless — and says the harvest is ready and the workers few. The sending has urgency: the field is not future tense. It is now, and it is full.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: See the harvest with compassion, not statistics
Volunteer as a worker — churches are full of spectators
Pray to the Lord of the harvest for more workers

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask the Lord of the harvest to raise up workers
Offer yourself as one

verse.text: And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.

blocks.text: The Great Commission ends not with a challenge but a presence: surely I am with you always. Today's quiz is on the grammar of the sending.

blocks.question: What makes the 'go' possible, according to Matthew 28:20?
options: Superior skills and strategy
His presence with you to the very end of the age
blocks.explain: Right — the sending is backed by the presence: 'I am with you always'. The mission runs on Emmanuel, not on competence.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive the promise: I am with you always
Let the Presence outpace your fear of going

verse.text: He makes me lie down in green pastures.

blocks.text: Sent ones need green pastures. The Shepherd doesn't only send; he makes his sheep lie down. On a rest day, let the sending pause so the sent one can be filled. You can't carry the message on an empty tank.

blocks.prompt: Where are you running to the neglected pasture? Write the rest you'll take this week so the sending can be sustained.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let the Shepherd make you lie down
Thank him for pastures on the way to the ends of the earth

verse.text: Therefore, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord.

blocks.text: Paul closes his great resurrection chapter with the sent one's posture: stand firm, let nothing move you, give yourselves fully. The work of the Lord is not wasted. On Monday, stand — sent, firm, and fully available.

blocks.prompt: Write the one 'sent' commitment you will carry out of this spring. Make it specific, dated, and yours.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to stand firm in the sending
Thank God your work in the Lord is never wasted

intro.text: The way of Jesus is a resurrection-way. This final week we walk in the hope that holds everything together — beyond crosses, beyond graves, beyond even the season ending.

verse.text: Why do you look for the living among the dead? He is not here; he has risen!

blocks.text: The resurrection is the hinge of the entire way. The tomb is empty not because of a trick but because death itself was outflanked. You do not worship a dead teacher; you follow a risen Lord. Everything you've walked this spring rests on that morning.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Re-announce the resurrection to yourself: he is not here, he is risen
Let the empty tomb rewrite one fear you're carrying
Stop looking for the living among the dead — including your own regrets

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rejoice in the risen Jesus
Ask to live as resurrection people, not grave visitors

verse.text: Because I live, you also will live.

blocks.text: His life is the source of yours — not 'he lived once' but 'he lives, and because he lives, you will live'. The hope that holds is not a memory but a presence. Your future is not a question mark; it is hitched to a risen Saviour.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let 'he lives' step on your anxiety today
Let the resurrection rewrite your view of your own ending
Live as someone with a future — because his is secured

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Hold to the risen Life who lives in you
Thank him that because he lives, you live

verse.text: Praise be to the God... who has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

blocks.text: Peter calls the hope 'living' — alive, growing, unkillable. Not the dead optimism of circumstance but a hope born through the resurrection and still pulsing. It is the hope that can't be talked out of you.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let the living hope survive one discouraging moment today
Name what you are hopeful for, grounded in the resurrection
Trace today's hope back to its birthday: he rose

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive the new birth into living hope
Thank God for hope that refuses to die

verse.text: You will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you.

blocks.text: The risen Jesus did not leave his people as orphans; he sent the Spirit — power for the witness, the joining, the long road. The hope that holds is not a bare idea; it is a Person empowering you daily.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Walk one step by the Spirit, not by sheer effort
Ask for power where you feel powerless
Co-operate with the Comforter — let him take the weight

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Welcome the Spirit of power into your day
Thank Jesus for not leaving you as an orphan

verse.text: Christ in you, the hope of glory.

blocks.text: Paul's mystery phrase: Christ in you, the hope of glory. Today's quiz is about where the hope that holds actually lives.

blocks.question: Where, literally, is the hope of glory to be found?
options: In Christ living in you
In a distant future you can only imagine
blocks.explain: Right — 'Christ in you is the hope of glory'. The hope isn't only ahead; it's already lodged in you.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive Christ in you as your hope of glory
Thank God for hiding glory in an earthen jar

verse.text: There remains, then, a Sabbath-rest for the people of God.

blocks.text: The resurrection secured a final rest, and the weekly rest foreshadows it. On a rest day, let the hope of the finished kingdom settle you — the God who rose guarantees the rest that remains. Even this season's labour will end in a Sabbath.

blocks.prompt: Write what Sabbath-rest in God's finished future does to your current striving. Spend a few quiet minutes receiving it now.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Enter the rest that remains
Thank God for a resurrection that settled the ending

verse.text: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death.

blocks.text: Thirteen weeks ends, but the way opens into forever. The last word of the Bible's hope: no more death, mourning, crying or pain — the first things have passed away, and the risen Lord's victory is complete. Carry that into the summer and beyond.

blocks.prompt: Write your closing prayer of the season — thanks for the walk, and hope for what the risen Jesus will do next in you.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Pray the hope that holds — no more tears, no more death
Thank the risen Jesus for this season, and for all that is still to come
